title: The URL host allowlist must still run when the secret scan has just failed
objective: In .github/workflows/ci.yml the `Secret scan` job runs `Validate secrets baseline`, then `Scan tracked files against baseline`, then `URL host allowlist`. The last step carries no `if:`, so its condition defaults to `success()` and GitHub SKIPS it whenever an earlier step in the job failed. MEASURED: `skipped` observed in three separate control runs during PR #81. The disclosure guard that keeps an internal package-feed hostname out of a PUBLIC repository therefore stops running at exactly the moment another guard has just fired - when the tree is known to be in an unexpected state and scrutiny should be highest. One finding hides the rest. This contradicts the rule the repository states in its own `dependencies` job comments and already follows in the `web` job added by PR #75.
evaluation_level_rationale: Level 2 is mandatory: this is a behaviour change to a security boundary (the guard enforcing that no internal hostname reaches a public repository), and it changes when a gate executes. A control that cannot be SHOWN to fail proves nothing, so every claim here is demonstrated at STEP level on real CI runs with the prediction recorded before the run, not inferred from the YAML.
measured_premise: scripts/check_urls.py is stdlib-only: it imports argparse, pathlib, re, subprocess, sys, shells out to `git ls-files -z`, and reads scripts/url-allowlist.txt plus the checkout. It has NO dependency on detect-secrets or on .secrets.baseline, so no state exists in which running it after those steps failed yields noise rather than a finding.

MEASURED on the clean tree at f033017: `python scripts/check_urls.py` reports 1260 URL(s), 57 distinct host(s), exit 0. That count is the impossible-value floor for this instrument - this repository can never legitimately contain zero URLs, so a near-zero reading means the enumeration broke, not that the tree is clean.

`.invalid` is ALREADY on the allowlist as a suffix rule (RFC 2606 reserved namespace), so `example.invalid` PASSES. The negative-control host for demonstration 3 must therefore be something else; a single-label token that is on neither the exact list nor any suffix rule is used instead, and it discloses nothing because it is not a hostname anyone owns.

detect-secrets 1.5.0 Base64HighEntropyString flags above a Shannon entropy of 4.5 over the base64 charset. The planted control string measures 5.0952 by that same formula, computed locally before any CI run was spent. The probe was validated with a negative control (a repeated-character string measuring 0.0000) so an all-TRIPS result is distinguishable from a broken instrument.
decision_always_vs_not_cancelled: `!cancelled()`, not `always()`. They differ on exactly one input - a CANCELLED run - and this workflow sets `concurrency: cancel-in-progress: true` keyed on `ci-${{ github.ref }}`, so that input occurs routinely: any second push to a branch cancels the run in flight. Under `always()` the step would execute inside that dying run, spending a runner on a result nobody will read and writing a step conclusion into a CANCELLED run, where a green step reads as 'the guard ran and passed' to anyone who does not also read the run conclusion. `cancelled` is not `failure`, and misreading one for the other has already bitten this project. `!cancelled()` retains the only behaviour this change needs - run after a FAILED step - and is the spelling the `web` and `dependencies` jobs already use, so the file gains no second idiom for the same intent.
in_scope: .github/workflows/ci.yml: add `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` to the `URL host allowlist` step of the `secrets` job, with a comment recording the measurement, the reason the condition is sound for THIS step, and the always()/!cancelled() choice.
.github/workflows/ci.yml: a comment on `Scan tracked files against baseline` recording why it is deliberately NOT given the same treatment (checked, not assumed).
out_of_scope_zero_diff: agent-state/feature_list.json - untouchable. F008 stays passes:false and no ledger flag is flipped.
tests/support/source_scan.py and tests/unit/test_secrets_baseline.py - the strict secrets route guard. If they go red, that is REPORTED, never repaired.
The `Scan tracked files against baseline` step's dependency on `Validate secrets baseline`. It is a REAL dependency (see findings) and changing it is outside the contract.
The `python` and `node` jobs' own masking edges. They are reported as findings; changing them is a separate slice.

Any npm command. `npm install` / `npm audit fix` rewrite lockfile `resolved` URLs to an internal package-feed host on this machine; committing one would leak internal infrastructure into a public repository.
The step ORDER in the secrets job. Unchanged - see findings.
acceptance_criteria: AC1 BEFORE, reproduced not cited: on main's ci.yml with the secret scan step failing, the `URL host allowlist` step conclusion is `skipped`.
AC2 AFTER: with the secret scan failing IDENTICALLY, the `URL host allowlist` step RUNS, and its own conclusion is reported.
AC3 AFTER: the `URL host allowlist` step can still go RED on its own merits - a URL on a non-allowlisted host makes it fail while the secret scan is green.
AC4 AFTER: a clean tree still passes - both steps `success` and the job `success`.
AC5 AFTER: the JOB still FAILS when the secret scan fails. `!cancelled()` must not turn a red job green; verified at JOB conclusion, not step conclusion.
AC6: the protected files are byte-identical to CURRENT main, proved by blob hash comparison rather than by `git diff --numstat`, which lies on this repository.
AC7: agent-state/progress.md is append-only, proved by RAW BYTE PREFIX against main's CURRENT byte count, with a negative control (one flipped byte must yield False).
verification_commands: gh run view <id> --json jobs -> read STEP conclusions by name, and the JOB conclusion separately
gh pr checks -> assert check-runs >= 5 and that jobs ran BY NAME (absence of red is not evidence of green)
negative_and_regression_tests: Demonstration 3 is the negative control on the guard itself: a guard that cannot be made to fail proves nothing.
The entropy probe carries its own negative control so an all-TRIPS reading cannot come from a broken instrument.
The append-only proof carries a flipped-byte negative control.

`gh --json ... --jq` can return a STRING ARRAY where .Length is a LINE COUNT and .Contains() is array membership; every such read is joined into one string first and carries a marker that MUST be absent, so an all-False result is distinguishable from a broken read.
data_security_privacy_portability_z0: No data, schema, migration or Z0 implication. Security: strictly increases the number of runs in which the disclosure guard executes; it removes no gate and weakens no check. Portability: none - a workflow condition. No secret, registry URL or internal hostname appears in any changed file, commit message, PR body or scratch artefact.
scratch_artefacts: Control branches and throwaway PRs are required to observe CI at step level, as PRs #75 and #81 also did. They are listed by name in the PR body for closing and are never merged.
boundary: Draft PR only. Do not merge. Do not modify agent-state/feature_list.json. F008 stays passes:false.
